title: Model-based approaches
text: common model bushmeat studies. safe harvest, called production \(P\), \[P = 0.6 \, K \, (\lambda_{\max} - 1) \, F.\] Reading piece piece: \(K\) density habitat can support (carrying capacity). \(0.6\,K\) density population assumed produce surplus. \(\lambda_{\max}\) fastest yearly growth species can manage. part \((\lambda_{\max} - 1)\) surplus adds year. \(F\) safety fraction depends long animal lives: 0.6 short-lived species (5 years), 0.4 medium-lived (5 10 years) 0.2 long-lived species (10 years). Long-lived animals bounce back slowly, take smaller share. lambda_max, can let package work three life-history numbers using ot_lambda_max(): number female young per female per year (b), age first reproduction () age last reproduction (w). solves Cole’s (1954) equation, \[1 = e^{-r} + b\,e^{-r } - b\,e^{-r (w + 1)}, \qquad \lambda_{\max} = e^{r}.\] Now model . pass life-history columns, lambda_max computed us, use lifespan set safety fraction \(F\).
code: ot_lambda_max(b = 0.55, a = 1, w = 10) #> [1] 1.542758 ot_pro(duiker_demography,        k = density_k,        harvest = annual_take,        b = b, a = a, w = w,        longevity = lifespan) #> model-based: Pro (Robinson & Redford production model) #>  #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   lambda_max     f limit observed ratio sustainable #> *      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>       #> 1       1.54   0.4 5.21       9    1.73 FALSE       #> 2       1.41   0.2 0.590      3.5  5.93 FALSE       #> 3       1.32   0.2 0.117      0.8  6.85 FALSE

text: ot_pbr() comes marine mammal management deliberately cautious. safe removal \[\mathrm{PBR} = N_{\min} \times \tfrac{1}{2} R_{\max} \times F_R,\] \(N_{\min}\) low, cautious estimate population size (-count), \(R_{\max}\) maximum yearly growth rate, \(F_R\) recovery factor 0.1 1 lower want extra careful. Give current abundance n coefficient variation cv, function works \(N_{\min}\) lower 20th percentile, \[N_{\min} = \frac{N}{\exp\!\left(0.842\sqrt{\ln(1 + CV^2)}\right)}.\] \(R_{\max}\) yearly (discrete) rate, \(\lambda_{\max} - 1\). rmax column instantaneous rate, convert fly, data masking allows:

text: Real environments steady. Good years bad years come go, variability eats much can safely take. ot_samse() follows idea, Manlik et al. (2022). projects population many times, growth slows near carrying capacity random good bad years, taking fixed number \(H\) year, \[N_{t+1} = \max\!\left(0,\; N_t \exp\!\left[r_{\max}\left(1 - \left(\tfrac{N_t}{K}\right)^{\theta}\right) + \varepsilon_t\right] - H\right), \qquad \varepsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_e).\] searches largest \(H\) keeps average yearly growth current size non-negative, keeping risk extinction 5% less. title: Model-based approaches
text: models treat landscape one pot. practice hunting spread evenly: heavy near villages light far away. ot_biode(), Levi et al. (2009, 2011), captures . settlement \(c\) spreads hunting effort around , strongest close fading distance \(\delta_c\): \[\varphi(\delta) = \frac{\exp\!\left(-\delta^2 / 2\sigma^2\right)}{2\pi\delta + 1},\] \(\sigma\) sets far hunters roam. \(P_c\) hunters, \(h\) hunts per hunter per year, encounter rate \(e\) kill probability \(d\), steady state density point map \[N(x, y) = \left[K^{\theta}\left(1 - \frac{e\,d\,h}{r}\sum_c P_c\,\varphi(\delta_c)\right)\right]_+^{1/\theta}.\] words: settlement presses animals around , population can still support whatever left carrying capacity \(K\). \([\,\cdot\,]_+\) means density go zero. Give study area extent (rectangle) boundary (polygon), areas shares refer real landscape arbitrary map size. summary reports study area (km²), area_extirpated share frac_extirpated, cpue, expected number kills per hunt. full predicted surface available ot_biode_surface(), ready mapping, catch per unit effort village ot_biode_cpue(). ggplot2 installed, surface maps nicely raster, depletion halos around settlements.

title: offtake: Sustainability Indices and Models for Wildlife Harvest and Hunting — offtake-package
text: Toolkit assessing sustainability wildlife exploitation (bushmeat hunting, recreational hunting fisheries). implements main index-based model-based approaches catalogued Adounke et al. (2026) doi:10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111606  reviewed Weinbaum et al. (2013) doi:10.1111/ele.12008 . Indices compare harvest abundance metric hunted reference sites: age structure comparison ('asc'), hunting yield comparison ('hyco') population density comparison ('pdc'). Models compare observed offtake estimated maximum sustainable harvest: production model Robinson Redford (1991) ('pro'), potential biological removal Wade (1998) doi:10.1111/j.1748-7692.1998.tb00688.x  ('pbr'), maximum sustainable yield logistic model ('msy'), spatially explicit source-sink model Levi et al. (2009, 2011) ('biode') stochastic extension PBR spirit Manlik et al. (2022) doi:10.1111/cobi.13897  ('samse').

title: Biodemographic spatial model of hunting depletion (Biode) — ot_biode
text: Predicts spatial distribution game density across landscape given location number hunters settlement, following spatially explicit model Levi et al. (2009), multi-settlement form (Levi et al. 2011). Unlike non-spatial models (ot_pro(), ot_pbr(), ot_msy()), Biode shows hunting depletes game: around settlements, remote areas stay close carrying capacity.

Remote, lightly hunted cells act sources resupply hunted sinks around settlements. Edges reflecting (animals leave grid), choice package; implementation published Levi et al. title: Maximum finite rate of population increase (Cole's equation) — ot_lambda_max
text: numeric vector, recycled length longest b, w, giving \(\lambda_{max}\) – maximum finite (per-year) rate increase. dimensionless greater 1 growing population (e.g. 1.30 means population can grow 30% per year). NA returned elements missing inputs positive root inside interval.

title: Maximum finite rate of population increase (Cole's equation) — ot_lambda_max
